thread:
Alex: FYI customer reported sudden p95 spikes on hosted API this morning. They sent a few request ids but want us to triage asap.
Maria (support): Can you drop the request ids + the exact model/region they hit? Also need a short repro plan (curl) and concurrency profile. customer said token counts ~600-800.
Alex: Here are the ids they gave: req_20260317_91, req_20260317_112, req_20260317_178. Model: rwd-small-7b, region: eu-west-1. They said load was a sustained 150 rps with concurrency 6 per client (3 clients).
Maria (support): Perfect. @Ken can you start a quick check for those request ids in logs? If we need a debug bundle I'll ask the customer to run the curl below and enable traces.
Ken (sre): Pulling logs now. Quick ask: collect the full request headers too if possible (auth id, content-length). Also need the time window — Alex when did this happen?
Alex: First seen 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z to 09:25:00Z. They've attached a sample prompt set (5 variants) and said average prompt ~420 tokens, response ~220 tokens.
Ken (sre): Ok. If logs don't show obvious resource contention we'll need a repro pack. Maria, please get them to run this curl once for each prompt in the set and return the --trace output or request ids from response headers.
Maria (support): I'll send this to them now. Add note about concurrency and token counts.
Maria (support): Message to customer: "Can you run one curl per prompt and paste the x-request-id from response headers and the curl --trace-ascii output? Also, can you run a short load of 30s at your production concurrency (6) and share the collected request ids? This helps us map slow requests to server-side traces."
Jordan (eng): If they can run a short stress, ask them to use our recommended stress script (small changes):

```
# example single-request reproducer
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small-7b","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":300}' \
  --trace-ascii ./trace_<PROMPT_ID>.txt

# for short sustained load use wrk or k6, concurrency 6, duration 30s, requests ~=150/s
```

Jordan (eng): Also ask them to include the exact client time skew and whether they used streaming. Streaming can hide latency symptoms.
Maria (support): Customer replied: they will run the single-request curl + a 30s run and send back x-request-ids. ETA 30m.
Ken (sre): Once we have ids I'll correlate to p95 spikes in the ingestion cluster and check KV cache hit rates + GPU utilization. If needed we'll request a debug bundle:

```
ri-collect debug-bundle --req-ids req_20260317_91,req_20260317_112,req_20260317_178 --since 2026-03-17T09:05:00Z --until 2026-03-17T09:30:00Z --out /tmp/reds-debug.tar.gz
```

Ken (sre): Heads-up: include the per-request GPU metrics (nvidia-smi snapshots) and any autoscale events around that window.
Maria (support): Customer sent back 12 x-request-ids from the 30s run. Pasting first few here: req_20260317_201, req_20260317_202, req_20260317_206. Trace files attached.
Ken (sre): Got them. Starting correlation. If we see a hot shard or a KV cache miss pattern we'll follow up with a reproducer that explicitly toggles caching off/on.
Alex: Also asked customer whether they have any recent changes: they rolled a new client version last week that increased tokenization pre-processing (might bump input size slightly).
Jordan (eng): Noted. If tokenization change increased average tokens, that can push sequences into a different kernel path and change perf. Will simulate locally with their exact prompt set and token counts.
Ken (sre): Early findings: several of the slow requests map to a specific host in eu-west-1 and show abrupt p95 CPU/GPU context switch patterns. Opening an incident thread if we confirm degradation.
Maria (support): Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated: collecting debug bundle and letting them know we're simulating with their promptset and concurrency. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Audit: ticket 98721 updated, priority -> high, responder -> Ken (sre).
